texts.preamble: Mohd Azmeire Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 9 February, 2022 Author: P.Naveen Rao Bench: P.Naveen Rao, G.Radha Rani Honourable Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao & Honourable Dr. Justice G.Radha Rani Writ Petition No.23505 Of 2021 Date: 09.02.2022 Between: Mohd.Azmeire Begum, w/o. Mohd. Afzal, Aged 40 years, occu:Housewife, r/o. H.No.17-2-156, Beerannakunta, Kareemabad, Warangal District. ..... Petitioner And The State of Telangana, rep.by its Prl.Secretary, General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, Secretariat, Hyderabad and others. .....Respondents The Court made the following: Pnr,J & Grr,J Wp No.23505 of 2021 2 Honourable Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao & Honourable Dr. Justice G.Radha Rani Writ Petition No.23505 Of 2021 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This writ petition is filed praying to grant the following relief: ".... to issue an appropriate Writ Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Habeas Corpus directing 3rd Respondent to produce the detenue, i.e., Adepu Anil @ Gumma now detained in Central Prison Warangal before this Hon'ble Court and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned detention order passed by the 2nd Respondent vide C.No.311/WRC/CSB-XI/2021 dated 28.05.2021 and confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1724 dated 31.07.2021 passed by the 1st Respondent as being illegal, arbitrary, improper, unilateral, unconstitutional and violative of Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India and to forthwith release the Detenue and to grant ..." 3. This writ petition is filed challenging the order of detention dated 28.05.2021 detaining the detenu on the ground that he was involved in Crime No.103 of 2021 of Inthezargunj Police Station, registered under Section 395 of the Indian Penal Code. The detaining authority also records that in addition to involvement of the detenu in the said crime, he was also involved in four crimes earlier registered against him, i.e., Crime No.130 of 2020 under Section 395 of IPC of Mills Colony Police Station, Crime No.131 of 2020 registered under Sections 395 and 427 of IPC of Mills Colony Police Station; Crime No.392 of 2019 registered under Section 394 read with Section 34 of IPC of Inthezargunj Police Station and Crime No.160 of 2017 under Section 302 of IPC of Zaffargadh Police Station. It was also noted that he was earlier detained under "The Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of PNR,J & GRR,J Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986), vide proceedings C.No.415/WRC/CSB-XI/2020, dated 2.6.2020.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for petitioner contends that on the allegation of involvement in solitary crime, it is not permissible to resort to preventively detain a person as required by the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986. A person can be detained preventively only if he is in the habit of involving in repeated crimes affecting public order. The order of preventive detention is only on the allegation of involvement of detenu in Crime No.103 of 2021, though there is reference to the earlier crimes alleged to have been committed by the detenu, but they are not relied upon and, therefore, for solitary crime preventive detention is not warranted. He further submits that Crime No.160 of 2017 and Crime No.392 of 2019 registered long ago and not being proximate to the order of detention, they could not have been relied upon to resort to preventively detain the detenu. He therefore submits that order of detention is ex facie illegal. Mohd Azmeire Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 9 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91794990/ 2 5. Learned Government Pleader for Home submits that as can be seen from the order of detention, even though the detenu was earlier detained by order dated 02.06.2020, after his release from detention, he resorted to commit further crimes and therefore it PNR,J & GRR,J would appear that the detenu is in the habit of committing crimes and, therefore, is not desirable to release him. His actions of repeatedly involving in crimes of dacoity and other crimes creating serious problem in maintaining overall law and order, and his actions are affecting the public order. Therefore, in order to prevent him from committing such crimes, the detention order was passed. 6. The detenu herein is also alleged to have committed offences in association with few other persons, against whom also orders of detention were passed. They have challenged the detention orders in Writ Petition Nos.23492, 23499 and 23504 of 2021.
